title: Lesser sept offices
summary: Minor posts young Garou can hold.

claims.text: Most lesser offices suit player characters because a sept can spare their holders now and then without losing strength.
A Garou may hold two or three minor offices, or one alongside a greater office, and elders often give them to young Garou to ease others’ burdens and teach responsibility.
The Caller of the Wyld invokes the sept’s totems at a moot, both the caern totem and the totems of every tribe present.

title: The birth of a metis
summary: What follows when a Garou breaks the Litany.

claims.text: Some mothers carrying a metis seek to end the pregnancy through Kinfolk or trusted packmates, and some go to desperate lengths.
Most werewolves who break the Litany part ways quickly, so a metis seldom has two parents raising it.

Hairless gives +1 difficulty to Social rolls in every form but Homid and bars dots in Pure Breed; Hooves and Horns also give +1 Social difficulty, though antlers may win Fianna respect for Stag and a single horn may impress the Children of Gaia.
Hard of Hearing gives +2 difficulty to Perception rolls involving sound, while full deafness removes hearing entirely and may impair speech.
Hemophilia stops the metis regenerating at all in combat, so healing needs a Gift such as Mother’s Touch.
A Human Face in every form brings +1 Social difficulty and may get the metis mistaken for a fomor or Black Spiral; Hunchback adds +1 to both Social and Dexterity rolls.
New Gifts include Wriggle, Frozen Form, Badger’s Heart and Twist of Fate.
Wriggle, taught by a Cockroach spirit, costs a Gnosis point and lets the metis squeeze into any space at least half its body size, in any form, for the scene.
Frozen Form, taught by any aerial spirit, draws on the metis’ years spent fixed in Crinos.
